```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

## Goal

Predict the total bases a batted ball produces (0, 1, 2, 3 or 4) from TrackMan
ball-flight measurements, and compare several models on a held-out test set.

I fit two versions of the final random forest:

- **Full model:** uses all six batted-ball measurements, including Distance and
  HangTime.
- **Contact-only model:** uses only ExitSpeed, Angle and Direction. Distance and
  HangTime describe where the ball ended up, so they partly reveal the result
  (a 400-foot fly ball is almost always a home run). MLB's expected stats use
  contact measurements for this reason, so this model is the fairer test of how
  well quality of contact alone predicts the outcome.

```{r libraries}
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)   # includes dplyr, tidyr and ggplot2
library(randomForest)
library(knitr)
```

## Data

The data file `trackman.xlsx` should sit in the same folder as this file.

```{r load-data}
data <- read_excel("trackman.xlsx")
```

```{r total-bases}
# Map PlayResult to total bases. Only hits add bases; every other result is 0.
numeric_playresult <- c(
  "Single" = 1,
  "Double" = 2,
  "Triple" = 3,
  "HomeRun" = 4,
  "-" = 0,
  "Walk" = 0,
  "Out" = 0,
  "Strikeout" = 0,
  "HitByPitch" = 0,
  "FieldersChoice" = 0,
  "Error" = 0,
  "Sacrifice" = 0,
  "Groundball" = 0
)

predictors         <- c("ExitSpeed", "Angle", "Direction", "HitSpinRate", "Distance", "HangTime")
contact_predictors <- c("ExitSpeed", "Angle", "Direction")

filtered_data <- data %>%
  mutate(total_bases = unname(numeric_playresult[PlayResult])) %>%
  select(all_of(predictors), total_bases) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ na_if(as.character(.x), "NA"))) %>%  # text "NA" -> real NA
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
  drop_na()  # keeps only batted balls with complete tracking data

nrow(filtered_data)
table(filtered_data$total_bases)
```

## Exploratory data analysis

```{r eda}
plot_fxn <- function(df, predictor) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = factor(total_bases), y = .data[[predictor]])) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    labs(title = paste(predictor, "by Total Bases"),
         x = "Total Bases",
         y = predictor) +
    theme_minimal()
}

for (p in predictors) print(plot_fxn(filtered_data, p))
```

## Train/test split

The seed is set before the split so the results are the same every time the file runs.

```{r split}
set.seed(203)
train_rows <- sample(nrow(filtered_data), size = floor(0.7 * nrow(filtered_data)))
train <- filtered_data[train_rows, ]
test  <- filtered_data[-train_rows, ]
```

## Choosing predictors: nested linear models

Each model adds one predictor. ANOVA tests whether the added predictor
significantly reduces the residual sum of squares.

```{r linear-anova}
mod1 <- lm(total_bases ~ ExitSpeed, data = train)
mod2 <- lm(total_bases ~ ExitSpeed + Angle, data = train)
mod3 <- lm(total_bases ~ ExitSpeed + Angle + Direction, data = train)
mod4 <- lm(total_bases ~ ExitSpeed + Angle + Direction + HitSpinRate, data = train)
mod5 <- lm(total_bases ~ ExitSpeed + Angle + Direction + HitSpinRate + Distance, data = train)
mod6 <- lm(total_bases ~ ExitSpeed + Angle + Direction + HitSpinRate + Distance + HangTime, data = train)

anova(mod1, mod2)
anova(mod2, mod3)
anova(mod3, mod4)
anova(mod4, mod5)
anova(mod5, mod6)
```

## Choosing polynomial degrees

For each predictor, fit polynomials of increasing degree and use ANOVA to see
which higher-order terms are worth keeping.

```{r poly-anova}
poly_anova <- function(predictor, max_degree) {
  fits <- lapply(1:max_degree, function(d) {
    lm(reformulate(sprintf("poly(%s, %d, raw = TRUE)", predictor, d), "total_bases"),
       data = train)
  })
  do.call(anova, c(fits, test = "Chisq"))
}

poly_anova("ExitSpeed",   5)
poly_anova("Angle",       5)
poly_anova("Direction",   5)
poly_anova("HitSpinRate", 4)
poly_anova("Distance",    5)
poly_anova("HangTime",    3)
```

## Models

```{r models}
# Empty model: predicts the training-set mean for every batted ball
test$empty_pred <- mean(train$total_bases)

# Linear model with the predictors kept by the nested ANOVA
linear_model <- lm(total_bases ~ ExitSpeed + HitSpinRate + Distance + HangTime, data = train)
test$linear_pred <- predict(linear_model, newdata = test)

# Polynomial model with the degrees chosen above
poly_model <- lm(total_bases ~
                   poly(ExitSpeed, 3, raw = TRUE) +
                   poly(HitSpinRate, 3, raw = TRUE) +
                   poly(Distance, 4, raw = TRUE) +
                   poly(HangTime, 2, raw = TRUE) +
                   poly(Angle, 4, raw = TRUE) +
                   poly(Direction, 2, raw = TRUE),
                 data = train)
test$poly_pred <- predict(poly_model, newdata = test)

# Interaction models: do two predictors work together?
interact_es_angle <- lm(total_bases ~ ExitSpeed * Angle,    data = train)
interact_es_dist  <- lm(total_bases ~ ExitSpeed * Distance, data = train)
interact_dist_ang <- lm(total_bases ~ Distance * Angle,     data = train)
test$es_angle_pred <- predict(interact_es_angle, newdata = test)
test$es_dist_pred  <- predict(interact_es_dist,  newdata = test)
test$dist_ang_pred <- predict(interact_dist_ang, newdata = test)

# Random forest, all six measurements
set.seed(203)
rf_full <- randomForest(reformulate(predictors, "total_bases"),
                        data = train, importance = TRUE)
test$rf_full_pred <- predict(rf_full, newdata = test)

# Random forest, contact measurements only (no Distance or HangTime)
set.seed(203)
rf_contact <- randomForest(reformulate(contact_predictors, "total_bases"),
                           data = train, importance = TRUE)
test$rf_contact_pred <- predict(rf_contact, newdata = test)
```

## Comparing models on the test set

RMSE is how far off the predictions are, on average, in bases. Lower is better.

```{r rmse}
rmse <- function(actual, predicted) sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2))
r_squared <- function(actual, predicted) {
  1 - sum((actual - predicted)^2) / sum((actual - mean(actual))^2)
}

pred_cols <- c(
  "Empty"                        = "empty_pred",
  "Linear"                       = "linear_pred",
  "Polynomial"                   = "poly_pred",
  "Exit Speed * Angle"           = "es_angle_pred",
  "Exit Speed * Distance"        = "es_dist_pred",
  "Distance * Angle"             = "dist_ang_pred",
  "Random Forest (all six)"      = "rf_full_pred",
  "Random Forest (contact only)" = "rf_contact_pred"
)

results <- tibble(
  Model   = names(pred_cols),
  RMSE    = sapply(pred_cols, function(col) rmse(test$total_bases, test[[col]])),
  Test_R2 = sapply(pred_cols, function(col) r_squared(test$total_bases, test[[col]]))
) %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

kable(results, digits = 4, col.names = c("Model", "RMSE", "Test R-squared"))
```

```{r rmse-plot}
ggplot(results, aes(x = reorder(Model, -RMSE), y = RMSE)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Model", y = "RMSE (bases)", title = "Test RMSE by Model") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Variable importance

Importance is the percent increase in MSE when a predictor's values are shuffled:
the bigger the increase, the more the model relies on that predictor.

```{r importance}
importance_df <- function(model, label) {
  tibble(Feature    = rownames(importance(model)),
         Importance = importance(model)[, "%IncMSE"],
         Model      = label)
}

bind_rows(importance_df(rf_full, "All six measurements"),
          importance_df(rf_contact, "Contact only")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Feature, Importance), y = Importance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ Model, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Random Forest Variable Importance",
       x = "Variable", y = "% Increase in MSE") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Save models

```{r save}
saveRDS(rf_full,    "rf_full_model.rds")
saveRDS(rf_contact, "rf_contact_model.rds")
```
